findings.area: Lifecycle fence / concurrency (publisher vs disable-uninstall drain)
findings.description: ArtworkPublisher.PublishCoreAsync reads the durable lifecycle fence exactly once, at the start, and never re-checks it before writing the Prepared operation, before the external SaveImage/image-removal call, or before committing the final PublishedArtworkState. ArtworkLifecycleCoordinator.DrainCoreAsync sets the fence and only then enumerates durable operations and Published states. A publication that observed Normal immediately before the fence was written can therefore durably record its Prepared operation after the drain has already enumerated operations, then mutate the image and commit Published after the drain has completed, so the drain reports Completed while the original artwork was not restored and an untracked publication survives the disable/uninstall fence. This cannot manifest in Phase 5 because no production caller drives PublishAsync (the generation/queue wiring is Phase 6), but it is a latent correctness gap in the core V1 lifecycle guarantee that must be closed before Phase 6 enables concurrent publication and lifecycle drains.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:173-179 (single fence read), :294 (Prepared write), :313-464 (no fence re-check before SaveImage/commit)
src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkLifecycleCoordinator.cs:137-233 (Set fence, then Enumerate operations and states)
src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkSubjectGate.cs:15-34 (serialization is per-subject, not global against the drain)
findings.recommended_action: Before Phase 6 drives this entry point, re-read and enforce the durable fence immediately before the first mutation and again before the final commit (abort/block on a non-normal fence), or add a drain/publication coordination barrier so the fence cannot be crossed by an in-flight publication. Add a test that interleaves a publication with DrainAsync.

findings.description: Task 5.9 changed the production Plugin constructor to take IServiceProvider (for the uninstall drain), but the packaged plugin has not been loaded on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host since that change. The last live-host package validation was task 5.4, which predates it. The assumption is supported: the pinned host constructs plugins with ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance(_appHost.ServiceProvider!, type), and Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection resolves IServiceProvider as a built-in service (independently reproduced with the pinned DI package: injection succeeds), so the constructor is host-compatible by framework semantics and pinned-host source. However, per the review rules, a build/test pass is not proof of the host lifecycle assumption; the actual package load path is unvalidated in its current form.
evidence: docs/implementation/5.9/worker-report.json known_limitations: 'No live-host ... validation was performed for this task' and the Plugin-constructor note
findings.recommended_action: Add a host-guarded construction/load fact (ActivatorUtilities over the real host service set) or re-run the package install/load on the pinned host, and record the result before or during Phase 6/7 host acceptance.

findings.description: ArrTags stores all authoritative state (PublishedArtworkState, ArtworkOperation, SourceArtifactStore bytes, lifecycle fence) under IPlugin.DataFolderPath. For a Jellyfin plugin that path is derived from the assembly location (plugins/<assemblyName>[_version]); catalog installs extract to plugins/<name>_<version> and older version folders are deleted on upgrade. If the plugin folder is the versioned install folder, an upgrade removes the retained source artifacts and ownership state while an ArrTags-published image may still be the active item image. ArrTags would then lose the ability to restore the original and, on the next publication, would capture its own output as a new source baseline (the exact failure ADR-002 seeks to prevent). Whether this occurs depends on the install layout (non-versioned manual install keeps a stable state root). This is a V1 release risk (GOALS success criterion 7 / Gate 7), not a Phase 5 execution gap.
findings.recommended_action: Track for Phase 7 install/upgrade/reload/uninstall validation. Validate upgrade behavior explicitly, and if state loss is confirmed, move the state root to a stable location or add a documented state-migration/preservation step; document the user-visible consequence from GOALS.md accordingly.

findings.description: No mechanism ever deletes artifact bytes. SourceArtifactStore is append-only, and StateRetention.ApplyAuthoritativeRetention deletes only terminal state JSON records, never the artifacts/source/*.bin bytes. Every distinct source and every distinct derived output accumulates, and SourceArtifactStore.Promote rejects new work once ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes is exceeded. Because the quota is authoritative storage that is never reclaimed, a busy item can permanently stop receiving new derived work (safe, but indefinitely degraded) until manual cleanup. ApplyRetention is also currently invoked only from tests, so even the terminal state pruning is not scheduled in production (expected before Phase 6).
evidence: grep: ApplyRetention is referenced only from tests, not from production wiring
findings.recommended_action: In Phase 6 add bounded artifact retention/GC that proves a candidate artifact is not the active image and not the retained session source before deletion, schedule ApplyRetention, and test quota reclamation on repeated publication.

findings.area: Cross-task integration (5.8 repeat publication / Phase 6 pipeline)
findings.description: ArtworkGenerationCoordinator always renders the observed active surface. When an ArrTags Published session already exists, that surface is the previous ArrTags output, so a repeat generation would derive from (and stack a badge onto) the previous derived image instead of the retained original source artifact (architecture section 9 step 4). Safety is preserved in Phase 5 because the coordinator is not wired to any invoker, the publisher reuses the retained source/ownership tokens, and the before-mutation revalidation aborts on external change, but the retained-source selection and repeat-publication gate must be implemented before Phase 6 drives the pipeline.
findings.recommended_action: Before Phase 6 invokes generation, add retained-source selection plus a fingerprint/idempotence gate for repeat publication, and test that a repeat publication renders from the retained original and does not double-badge.

findings.area: Test coverage carried forward from Phase 4 (configuration to render)
findings.description: The Phase 4 review's MEDIUM integration-test finding remains open: there is still no end-to-end test that builds a PluginConfiguration with an overridden palette and a disabled selector, resolves it through PluginConfigurationSnapshot, and renders with the resolved definitions/policy. RendererConfigurationTests still validates only snapshot-level resolution; the render tests use BadgeDefinition.V1Default and RenderOutputPolicy.Default. Phase 5 now feeds snapshot-derived definitions into new paths, so this gap is more relevant.
findings.recommended_action: Add the configuration-to-render integration test in Phase 6 when renderer configuration is wired to the administrative save/config surface.

findings.description: ArtworkSubjectGate is a process-wide static ConcurrentDictionary keyed by item id + surface. Entries (SemaphoreSlim + string key) are created lazily and never removed, so a large library processed over time accumulates one entry per processed subject permanently. This is bounded by the number of subjects ever processed but is unbounded in the sense that removal/item-deletion never releases the entry.
findings.recommended_action: Track for Phase 6: prune idle per-subject gates (for example reference-count or weak-cache them), or document the bound as accepted.

findings.description: Artwork singletons (IArtworkImageAccess, IArtworkSourceReader, ArtworkPublisher, StateRepository) capture OperationalLimits from ConfigurationSnapshotService.Current at first resolution and never refresh them. A runtime configuration replacement (changed source/derived/storage limits) is therefore not applied to the artwork boundary until process restart. A stale larger limit is still re-checked against the render request; a stale smaller limit fails conservatively. The 5.3 reviewer noted the same pattern.
findings.recommended_action: When limits become user-tunable (Phase 6 / DG-6), resolve limits per operation from the current snapshot rather than capturing them at singleton construction, or document the restart-required behavior.

findings.description: StopAsync's drain bound is cooperative: it links the shutdown token and sets CancelAfter(15s) but awaits the coordinator directly, so a host API that ignores cancellation could extend shutdown. Plugin.OnUninstalling similarly blocks the uninstall thread on a bounded synchronous wait. All in-repo awaits honor the token, so the documented bound holds in practice. This is a defense-in-depth note, not an observed defect (5.9 reviewer F4).
findings.recommended_action: Consider Task.WaitAsync for a hard bound if a real host path is found to ignore cancellation; otherwise retain as documented.

findings.description: ReconstructPublicationSession's fallback (used when the associated Published state is absent for a non-terminal publication) sets SourceFingerprint = operation.SourceArtifactId while SourceCaptureIdentity = operation.ExpectedBeforeIdentity. For a repeat publication these disagree (expected-before is the prior derived image; source fingerprint is the original source hash), so PublishedArtworkState.Validate rejects the reconstructed state and CompleteAfterRecovery enters RecoveryBlocked after the image was already updated. The outcome is fail-closed and the normal crash/restart paths reconstruct consistently, so this is an edge-case robustness gap (5.7 reviewer F5).
findings.recommended_action: Reconstruct the source capture identity from the retained source artifact (not expectedBefore) when a prior publication is implied, and add a targeted test.

findings.description: PNG/JPEG confinement is enforced in the host adapter and re-checked in ArtworkSourceReader, but SourceImageInput still accepts any content type beginning with 'image/'. A future caller that builds a SourceImageInput without going through IArtworkSourceReader could reintroduce the Phase 4 color-profile fail-open gap for an uninspected container. The supported path is closed (5.3), and the renderer was intentionally not modified.
findings.recommended_action: Track as a hardening item: narrow SourceImageInput/SourceImageDescriptor acceptance to the inspected containers, or add a guard at the renderer input boundary.

findings.description: The task 5.11 publish-then-read-back case uses the real JellyfinArtworkImageWriter but a DispatchProxy IProviderManager whose OnStreamSave callback writes the derived temp file and replaces item.ImageInfos; it does not exercise the real host ImageSaver or the host's actual on-disk image representation. The test therefore proves the route/writer contract given that item state, not that the real ImageSaver produces it. The limitation is disclosed in the worker report and research section 4.4; no live HTTP round-trip was performed and the Phase 6 generation-to-publication pipeline is not wired.
findings.recommended_action: Close with a live-host acceptance check (package install + real ImageSaver + HTTP GET) in Phase 6/7.

findings.description: On the Published/NotPublished repeat-publication path the publisher reuses state.SourceArtifactId without reading or integrity-validating the retained source artifact, so a corrupt or missing retained source is not detected at that point (rendering is out of publisher scope and the Phase 6 render path would fail first). Not an acceptance gap, but the source integrity check is stronger in the restoration path than in the repeat-publication path.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Artwork/ArtworkPublisher.cs:225-298 (state reuse path), :1365-1403 (artifact validation only on recovery)
findings.recommended_action: Optionally validate the retained source artifact when reusing a published session, or rely on the Phase 6 pipeline gate and document the assumption.

findings.description: Several documents remain stale or imprecise relative to the completed implementation: (a) docs/implementation-readiness.md Status line 5 does not record Phase 5 completion, and its deferred-item text still says 'the live-host behavior of the packaged assets remain Phase 5 validation' (task 5.4 performed that validation) and 'the exact publication read-back remains host validation'; (b) implementation-readiness.md:43 still attributes the EXIF defect to 'orientations 5-8' although orientation 5 was already correct (Phase 4 review LOW); (c) docs/architecture.md:3 still reads 'Phase 1 complete'; (d) docs/architecture.md:754 summarises 'failure returns pass-through' while the renderer returns a bounded Failed for decode/limit/contrast/encode cases (ADR-010 permits both); (e) docs/data-model.md 3.7 lists RenderRequest.requestId and imageSurface as fields while the mapping table 4.7 marks them Not applicable to the implemented contract. None of these affect behavior.
findings.recommended_action: Update the readiness status/deferred wording, the orientation wording, the architecture status/failure wording, and the data-model RenderRequest note in the next documentation pass. PLANS.md, README.md, and docs/changelog.md already state Phase 5 completion/Gate 5 consistently at the integration-test level.

summary: Phase 5 (Jellyfin artwork integration) is complete and independently verified. All eleven tasks in the authoritative execution order are complete, each with worker and reviewer evidence and a commit, and the commit order exactly matches the execution order; the working tree is clean. The implementation conforms to ADR-001/002/003/009/010/011, data-model 3.10.1-3.10.4, and architecture section 9/10: a Jellyfin-free renderer, host-confined source/read and image-mutation adapters, a content-addressed source store, a durable generation-fenced ArtworkOperation write-ahead journal, a single deterministic publication/restoration executor, postcondition reconciliation, a durable lifecycle fence with guarded restoration and item-removal tombstoning, and the ADR-011 Enhanced coexistence policy. I independently built the solution (0 warnings/0 errors) and ran the suites: the default run reproduced 973 passed / 58 skipped / 1031 total and the host-guarded run reproduced 987 passed / 44 skipped / 1031 total, matching the claims. Gate 5 is met for the pinned 12.0.0 ABI at the integration-test level as the phase scopes it: the real pinned ImageController route/response pipeline and the real ArrTags image-mutation boundary pass, and source preservation/restoration is demonstrated. No BLOCKER or HIGH finding was identified; the residual items are MEDIUMs (a latent lifecycle-fence race between publication and the disable/uninstall drain that only becomes reachable once Phase 6 drives publication; the plugin IServiceProvider constructor change not re-validated by an actual pinned-host load since task 5.9, though framework semantics confirm it; provenance loss on plugin upgrade when the state root is the versioned plugin folder; no artifact garbage collection so the authoritative quota is never reclaimed; the deferred repeat-publication retained-source selection; and the still-open Phase 4 configuration-to-render integration test) plus LOW notes (unpruned per-subject gate dictionary, limits captured at singleton construction, cooperative shutdown bound, a state-loss recovery edge, SourceImageInput confinement hardening, the double-backed 5.11 read-back, repeat-publication source-integrity, and documentation staleness). Phase 5 is approved and Phase 6 may proceed, with the MEDIUM items tracked for Phase 6/7.
